title: Meraki Exporter Health
description: Is the exporter itself working? Collector success, poll freshness, and API budget from meraki-exporter. Deliberately has no Network filter: none of these metrics carry network labels, because they describe the exporter and the organization rather than any site.

panels.title: Scrape Target Up
panels.description: up{job=~"meraki.*"} across every Meraki scrape job. 0 means Prometheus cannot reach the exporter at all, in which case every other panel here is showing stale data or nothing.

panels.title: Collectors Failing
panels.description: Collectors whose last run returned an error. A collector that fails reports nothing for its whole dataset, so this going above zero means metrics are missing somewhere — see the table below for which. Note a DISABLED collector emits no series at all and cannot appear here; check COLLECTORS_ENABLED if something is missing while this reads 0.

panels.title: Collectors Running
panels.description: How many collectors are enabled and reporting. Compare against COLLECTORS_ENABLED: a lower number means a collector is switched off, which produces no failure signal anywhere.

panels.title: Fast Poll Age
panels.description: Time since the fast group last completed a poll. Thresholds match MerakiExporterFastGroupStale (critical above 15m, which is 3x a 5m poll interval).

panels.title: Slow Poll Age
panels.description: Time since the slow group last completed a poll. Thresholds match MerakiExporterSlowGroupStale (warning above 90m). If this reads No Data, no collectors are assigned to the slow group at all.

panels.title: Organization
panels.description: Which organization this exporter is monitoring, from meraki_org_info. An empty name means the configured MERAKI_ORG_ID is not visible to the API key — the exporter warns once and then keeps running while producing failures.

panels.title: Collector Success Over Time
panels.description: 1 = the collector's last run succeeded, 0 = it failed. Drops to 0 mean that collector's entire dataset was missing for that period. A line disappearing entirely means the collector was disabled or the exporter restarted without it.

panels.title: Collector Status Now
panels.description: Current state of every enabled collector. Anything reading FAILING is reporting no data for its whole dataset.

panels.title: Collector Duration
panels.description: How long each collector's last run took. Watch this against the poll interval of its group: a collector approaching its interval will start having polls aborted. The clients collector is the usual first offender because it makes one API call per network.

panels.title: Poll Age by Group
panels.description: Seconds since each poll group last completed. Should saw-tooth up to roughly the group's interval and reset. A line that climbs without resetting means that group has stopped polling.

panels.title: Exporter API Requests by Status Code
panels.description: Requests this exporter makes to the Meraki API, by HTTP status. 429s mean it is being rate limited — the client self-limits to about 5 req/s, half the per-org budget, so sustained 429s usually mean another consumer is using the same budget.

panels.title: Org-wide API Response Codes (24h window)
panels.description: Counts across ALL API consumers in the organization, not just this exporter, over a rolling 24h window — so it is a slow-moving total rather than a rate. A rising 429 line with a flat exporter 429 line on the left means someone else is eating the budget. Requires the apiusage collector.
